evals.prompt: parsetree/ parses a file of whitespace-separated integers into a binary search tree (build: `cc -O2 -std=c17 -o pt parsetree/*.c`, input: `sh parsetree/gen.sh > in.txt`, run: `./pt in.txt`). Instruments puts malloc and free at about 30% of CPU for the 2-million-key input. Cut the allocator cost without leaking and without changing the printed results, the behavior on malformed input, or the API in parsetree/tree.h. The build compiles every .c file in parsetree/, so leave only shipped sources there. Tell me the allocator call counts and the run time before and after.
evals.expected_output: Nodes come from an arena (or equivalent bulk allocator) released in tree_free, results and NULL-on-error behavior are unchanged, an allocator-call count and repeated timings are reported for baseline and candidate, and the oracle ran under ASan/UBSan or is stated as not run.

assertions.text: A check-owned harness gets the original's count, height, and checksum for empty, whitespace-only, duplicate, LONG_MIN/LONG_MAX, and 200000-key inputs, NULL for malformed and out-of-range tokens, and no allocation live after tree_free or a failed parse.
tree_parse makes at most 2000 counted allocator calls (malloc, calloc, realloc, aligned_alloc, posix_memalign) for 200000 keys, down from the original's 200001.

assertions: The reply reports allocator call counts for baseline and candidate, from a counting wrapper, Instruments Allocations, or an equivalent tool that was actually run.
The reply reports before and after timings from the same -O2 build and machine with repeated runs (hyperfine or a timing loop), not a single run.
The reply states the result of an ASan/UBSan oracle run over the candidate, or states that it was not run.

evals.prompt: Our CSV exporter (C17, clang -O2) is slow. `sample` shows 85% of time in strcat under build_line(): `char line[65536]; line[0] = 0; for (size_t i = 0; i < ncols; i++) { strcat(line, cols[i]); strcat(line, ","); }`. Then each line goes out with `write(fd, line, strlen(line))`. Make it faster without changing the output bytes.
evals.expected_output: An end-offset join with memcpy and a computed length check, batched writes with a partial-write loop, an oracle comparing output bytes (cksum) on empty, one-column, and UTF-8 input, and hyperfine or timing-loop numbers before and after.
assertions: Replaces the repeated strcat with a tracked end offset (memcpy or equivalent) and checks that the total length fits the buffer.
Batches output into a buffer written with a loop that handles partial writes and EINTR, or uses stdio full buffering.
Compares baseline and candidate output bytes (cksum, cmp, or an oracle) including empty and multi-byte input.
Reports before/after measurements from the same build flags and machine with repeats, not a single run.

evals.prompt: Add `restrict` to every pointer parameter in src/image.c to speed it up. One function is `void blend(uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *a, const uint8_t *b, size_t n)` and callers sometimes pass dst == a for in-place blending.
evals.expected_output: The agent refuses to add restrict to blend because an in-place call aliases dst and a (undefined behavior), audits call sites before adding restrict elsewhere, and verifies any change with -S or remarks plus a timing comparison.
assertions: States that restrict on blend is undefined behavior for the dst == a call and does not apply it there.
Audits call sites for overlap before adding restrict to any other function.
Uses -S assembly, optimization remarks, or timing to show a benefit before keeping any restrict change.

evals.prompt: Turn on -ffast-math globally in our Makefile so the sum loop in stats.c vectorizes. stats.c also has `if (isnan(x)) continue;` to skip missing values.
evals.expected_output: The agent rejects global -ffast-math because finite-math makes NaN handling undefined and would break the isnan filter, and offers a scoped #pragma clang fp reassociate(on) on the sum loop (or explicit accumulators) verified with -S (fadd.4s) or remarks and a tolerance-based oracle.
assertions: Explains that -ffast-math implies finite-math and makes the isnan check unreliable.
Proposes a scoped alternative (#pragma clang fp reassociate or explicit accumulators) limited to the reduction.
Verifies vectorization with -S or optimization remarks rather than assuming it.
Notes that the summation order and therefore rounding change and tests with a tolerance or exact inputs.

evals.prompt: Our release build ships to customers' x86-64 servers of mixed age. A teammate wants `-march=native` in CFLAGS because the build server has AVX-512 and a checksum loop got 2x faster there.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that -march=native binaries can fault with illegal instructions on older CPUs, proposes an explicit baseline (-march=x86-64-v2/v3 matching the fleet) or runtime dispatch with __attribute__((target)) and __builtin_cpu_supports, and requires testing on the oldest supported CPU.
assertions: States that -march=native can produce illegal-instruction crashes on older fleet CPUs.
Offers runtime dispatch (target attribute plus __builtin_cpu_supports) or an explicit baseline level instead.
Requires the oracle and timing on the oldest supported CPU or states that it was not verified.

evals.prompt: Reformat the C sources in stats/ with clang-format (stats/.clang-format is our style) and fix the -Wshadow warnings the Makefile build prints. No behavior or performance changes.
evals.expected_output: Sources pass clang-format, the build is warning-free under -Wshadow, the program prints the same line, and the Makefile flags and code carry no optimization changes.

assertions.text: clang-format --dry-run --Werror reports no violations in stats/.
assertions.check:
command -v clang-format >/dev/null || { echo 'FAIL: clang-format not found on PATH'; exit 1; }
clang-format --dry-run --Werror stats/*.c stats/*.h

assertions.text: stats/ builds with -Wall -Wshadow -Werror and prints the original line `mean=5.000 variance=4.000 above4=4 records=9`.
The Makefile's CFLAGS line is unchanged and no restrict, pragma, attribute, inline, or branch-hint constructs were added.
assertions.check:
grep -qx 'CFLAGS = -O2 -std=c17 -Wall -Wshadow' stats/Makefile || { echo 'FAIL: CFLAGS in stats/Makefile changed'; exit 1; }
if grep -Eq '\brestrict\b|__builtin_expect|#pragma|__attribute__|\binline\b' stats/*.c stats/*.h; then echo 'FAIL: optimization constructs added'; exit 1; fi
